items.definition: Logistics is the planning and control of the movement and storage of goods, services and related information, from where they come from to where they are needed, so they arrive at the right place, time, quantity, condition and cost.
items.definition_ar: اللوجستيات هي تخطيط وإدارة حركة وتخزين البضائع والمعلومات المرتبطة بها من مصدرها إلى مكان الحاجة إليها، بحيث تصل في المكان والوقت والكمية والحالة والتكلفة الصحيحة.
items.explanation: Logistics covers transport, warehousing, inventory holding, packaging, order handling and the information that goes with them. It is one part of supply chain management: logistics executes the physical and information flows that the wider supply chain plans and coordinates across companies.
items.example: Booking a 40ft container from Antwerp to Tema, storing the spare parts in a bonded warehouse and delivering them to a mine site are logistics activities.
misconceptions: Logistics is not only trucking or transport: storage, inventory and information are part of it.
Logistics and supply chain management are not the same thing (see the related item).

sources.note: The topic is defined in the ASCM dictionary; this wording is ATLAS's own.

items.definition: Supply chain management is the design, planning, execution and control of the whole network that turns supplier inputs into products delivered to customers — sourcing, making, moving, storing and returning — coordinated across the companies involved.
items.definition_ar: إدارة سلاسل الإمداد هي تصميم وتخطيط وتنفيذ ومراقبة الشبكة الكاملة من الموردين حتى العملاء: الشراء والتصنيع والنقل والتخزين والمرتجعات، بالتنسيق بين كل الشركات المشاركة.
items.explanation: The difference that matters in practice: logistics moves and stores the goods; supply chain management decides what to buy, from whom, how much to hold, where to make it and how the partners share plans and risk. A late container is a logistics problem; deciding to dual-source a part because one supplier's lead time is unreliable is a supply chain decision.
items.example: Mantrac choosing to stock fast-moving Caterpillar filters locally while ordering rare parts on demand is a supply chain decision; arranging the airfreight for an urgent part is logistics.
misconceptions: SCM is not just a newer name for logistics: it includes procurement, planning and supplier relationships.

items.definition: Inbound logistics is the flow of goods and information from suppliers into the company: purchase-order follow-up, transport, import clearance, receiving and putting the goods into stock.
items.definition_ar: اللوجستيات الواردة هي تدفق البضائع والمعلومات من الموردين إلى الشركة: متابعة أوامر الشراء والنقل والتخليص الجمركي للوارد والاستلام والتخزين.
items.explanation: For a dealer such as Mantrac most imported equipment and parts are inbound flows: the supplier ships, a forwarder moves the cargo, customs clears it at the destination and the branch receives it. The ETA/ATA automation in this platform works on inbound shipments that are Under Clearance.
items.example: A Caterpillar engine shipped from the US to Lagos and received into the Lagos warehouse.

items.definition: Outbound logistics is the flow of finished goods and information from the company to its customers: order processing, picking and packing, transport and delivery.
items.definition_ar: اللوجستيات الصادرة هي تدفق البضائع الجاهزة والمعلومات من الشركة إلى العملاء: معالجة الطلبات والتجهيز والتعبئة والنقل والتسليم.
items.explanation: Outbound performance is what the customer sees (on-time delivery, damage, completeness), so its KPIs are usually measured against a promised date.
items.example: Delivering a serviced generator from a branch workshop to a customer's site.

items.definition: Procurement is obtaining the goods and services a company needs: finding and selecting suppliers, agreeing terms (including the Incoterms rule), placing purchase orders and following them up until receipt and payment.
items.definition_ar: المشتريات هي الحصول على ما تحتاجه الشركة من سلع وخدمات: اختيار الموردين والتفاوض على الشروط (ومنها قاعدة الإنكوترمز) وإصدار أوامر الشراء ومتابعتها حتى الاستلام والدفع.
items.explanation: Procurement decisions set the logistics that follow: the Incoterms rule chosen in the purchase decides who books the main transport, who insures, and where the risk passes to the buyer.
items.example: Buying parts FCA supplier's warehouse means the buyer's forwarder collects them and the buyer arranges the main carriage.

items.definition: Order fulfillment is everything between receiving a customer's order and the customer having the goods: checking stock, allocating, picking, packing, shipping, delivering and confirming.
items.definition_ar: تنفيذ الطلبات هو كل ما يحدث بين استلام طلب العميل ووصول البضاعة إليه: التحقق من المخزون والتخصيص والتجهيز والتعبئة والشحن والتسليم والتأكيد.
items.explanation: Fulfillment performance is measured from the order (order cycle time, OTIF), not from when the truck left.

items.definition: Distribution is moving finished goods from where they are made or stocked to the places and customers that need them, through a network of warehouses, branches and transport links.
items.definition_ar: التوزيع هو نقل البضائع الجاهزة من أماكن تصنيعها أو تخزينها إلى الأماكن والعملاء الذين يحتاجونها عبر شبكة من المخازن والفروع ووسائل النقل.
items.explanation: A distribution network trades holding cost against service: more stocking points mean faster delivery and more inventory.

items.definition: Reverse logistics is the flow of goods back from customers or sites: returns, warranty parts, repairable components, reusable packaging and items for recycling or disposal.
items.definition_ar: اللوجستيات العكسية هي تدفق البضائع عكسيًا من العملاء أو المواقع: المرتجعات وقطع الضمان والمكونات القابلة للإصلاح والعبوات المعاد استخدامها والمواد المعاد تدويرها.
items.explanation: Returns crossing a border are often re-exports or temporary exports and need their own customs treatment; they cannot simply ride on the original import paperwork.
items.example: Sending a failed component back to the manufacturer for warranty analysis (a core return).

items.definition: The shipper (consignor) is the party that hands the goods over for carriage and is named as shipper on the transport document — usually the seller or its agent.
items.definition_ar: الشاحن هو الطرف الذي يسلم البضاعة للنقل ويُذكر كشاحن في مستند النقل، وغالبًا البائع أو وكيله.
items.explanation: The shipper on the bill of lading is not always the seller (a forwarder may ship on its behalf), and is not necessarily the party paying the freight — that follows the Incoterms rule and the freight terms (prepaid or collect).
misconceptions: The shipper is not always the party who pays the freight.

items.definition: The consignee is the party named on the transport document to receive the goods at destination — usually the buyer, its agent or a bank.
items.definition_ar: المرسل إليه هو الطرف المذكور في مستند النقل لاستلام البضاعة في الوجهة، وعادة المشتري أو وكيله أو بنك.
items.explanation: For a negotiable 'to order' bill of lading the consignee field may say 'to order' or name a bank; the party that can take delivery is whoever presents the properly endorsed original. The notify party is only informed of arrival.

items.definition: The notify party is the party the carrier tells when the goods arrive — often the buyer or its customs broker. Being the notify party does not by itself give a right to take delivery.
items.definition_ar: الطرف المُخطَر هو من يبلغه الناقل بوصول البضاعة، وغالبًا المشتري أو مخلصه الجمركي، ولا يعطيه ذلك وحده حق استلام البضاعة.

items.definition: The carrier is the company that contracts to transport the goods and issues (or has issued for it) the transport document: a shipping line, an airline, a trucking or rail operator.
items.definition_ar: الناقل هو الشركة التي تتعاقد على نقل البضاعة وتُصدر مستند النقل: خط ملاحي أو شركة طيران أو شركة نقل بري أو سكك حديدية.
items.explanation: An actual carrier physically moves the cargo; a contracting carrier (for example an NVOCC or a forwarder issuing its own house document) takes carrier responsibility without owning the ship or plane. Tracking normally works with the actual carrier's reference (master B/L or master AWB).

items.definition: A freight forwarder arranges transport for its customer: it books carriers, consolidates cargo, prepares or collects documents and often arranges customs clearance, insurance and delivery.
items.definition_ar: وكيل الشحن يرتب النقل لعميله: يحجز مع الناقلين ويجمّع الشحنات ويجهز المستندات وغالبًا يرتب التخليص الجمركي والتأمين والتوصيل.
items.explanation: A forwarder may act as an agent (arranging carriage on the customer's behalf) or as a principal issuing its own house bill of lading or house air waybill, in which case it takes a carrier's responsibility to the customer. FIATA is the international federation of forwarders' associations.

items.definition: A customs broker (clearing agent) is licensed to lodge customs declarations and handle clearance on an importer's or exporter's behalf.
items.definition_ar: المخلص الجمركي مرخص لتقديم الإقرارات الجمركية وإنهاء إجراءات التخليص نيابة عن المستورد أو المصدر.
items.explanation: Licensing and liability rules are national. In the eHub clearance export each shipment names its clearing agent, and ATLAS uses that name to find who to contact about a past-due step.

items.definition: An NVOCC is a carrier that issues its own bills of lading and takes carrier responsibility to its shippers but does not operate the vessels; it buys space from shipping lines.
items.definition_ar: الـ NVOCC ناقل يُصدر بوالص شحن خاصة به ويتحمل مسؤولية الناقل أمام عملائه لكنه لا يشغّل السفن، بل يشتري مساحات من الخطوط الملاحية.
items.explanation: With an NVOCC there are two bills of lading: the line's master B/L to the NVOCC and the NVOCC's house B/L to the shipper. The line's tracking uses the master reference; the house number may mean nothing to the line.

items.definition: A 3PL is an outside company that performs logistics operations for a client — transport, warehousing, distribution, sometimes customs — usually under a contract with service levels.
items.definition_ar: مزود الخدمات اللوجستية الخارجي (3PL) شركة خارجية تنفذ العمليات اللوجستية لعميلها مثل النقل والتخزين والتوزيع وأحيانًا الجمارك، عادة بعقد ومستويات خدمة محددة.

items.definition: A 4PL manages a client's whole logistics operation, including the 3PLs and carriers that execute it, acting as a single integrator and usually owning few physical assets.
items.definition_ar: مزود الطرف الرابع (4PL) يدير منظومة اللوجستيات كاملة للعميل بما فيها مزودي 3PL والناقلين، كمنسّق واحد غالبًا دون أصول مادية كثيرة.
items.explanation: The line between a large 3PL and a 4PL is blurred in practice; the distinguishing idea is managing other providers rather than executing the work.

items.definition: An order is what was bought (one purchase order, many lines). A shipment is a quantity of goods moved together under one transport document. A consignment is the goods sent from one shipper to one consignee; in practice it is often used as a synonym for shipment.
items.definition_ar: الطلبية هي ما تم شراؤه (أمر شراء بعدة بنود). الشحنة هي كمية تُنقل معًا بمستند نقل واحد. الإرسالية هي البضاعة المرسلة من شاحن واحد إلى مرسل إليه واحد، وتُستخدم عمليًا كمرادف للشحنة.
items.explanation: One order can travel in several shipments (split delivery), and one shipment can carry several orders (consolidation). Matching them is a common source of reconciliation errors: a shipment can be 'arrived' while its order is only partly delivered. In this platform a shipment is identified by its BOL/AWB number.

definitions.text: A shipment is what one transport document (B/L or AWB) covers.
An order is a purchase order; its lines may be shipped separately.

misconceptions: One PO is not always one shipment, and one shipment is not always one PO.

items.definition: Cargo is the goods being carried. Freight means either the goods carried (mostly in American usage) or the charge paid for carrying them (as in 'freight prepaid').
items.definition_ar: البضاعة (Cargo) هي ما يُنقل. أما Freight فتعني البضاعة المنقولة أو أجرة النقل نفسها (مثل freight prepaid أي أجرة مدفوعة مقدمًا).
items.explanation: Read 'freight' from context: 'freight charges' and 'freight collect' refer to the price; 'freight train' to the goods.

items.definition: Delivery is the hand-over of the goods to the party entitled to receive them, at the agreed place. Under the Incoterms rules 'delivery' has a narrower meaning: the point where the seller has fulfilled its obligation to deliver and risk passes to the buyer.
items.definition_ar: التسليم هو تسليم البضاعة للطرف المستحق في المكان المتفق عليه. وفي قواعد الإنكوترمز للتسليم معنى أضيق: النقطة التي يكون البائع عندها قد أوفى بالتزامه وتنتقل المخاطر إلى المشتري.
items.explanation: Under FOB the seller 'delivers' when the goods are on board at the port of shipment, weeks before anyone at destination would call them delivered. Ask which meaning is meant.

definitions.text: Hand-over to the consignee at the final destination, shown by a proof of delivery.
The point where the seller's delivery obligation is met and risk passes; it depends on the rule.

sources.note: Delivery and risk transfer are defined per rule in the ICC text; summarised here.

items.definition: Inventory is the stock a company holds — raw materials, spare parts, finished goods and goods in transit — to meet demand and absorb uncertainty in supply and demand.
items.definition_ar: المخزون هو ما تحتفظ به الشركة من مواد خام وقطع غيار وبضائع جاهزة وبضائع في الطريق لتلبية الطلب وامتصاص عدم اليقين في الإمداد والطلب.
items.explanation: Safety stock covers variability; its size grows with lead-time uncertainty. That is why unreliable ETAs cost money even when nothing is lost: planners hold more stock to cover them. Goods in transit are inventory too, owned by whoever holds title under the sale contract.

items.definition: Warehousing is receiving, storing, protecting and dispatching goods. A bonded warehouse holds imported goods under customs control with duty not yet paid.
items.definition_ar: التخزين هو استلام البضائع وحفظها وحمايتها وصرفها. المخزن الجمركي (Bonded) يحفظ البضائع المستوردة تحت رقابة الجمارك قبل سداد الرسوم.
items.explanation: Bonded storage defers duty until goods are released for home use; the rules for how long goods may stay and what may be done to them are national.

items.definition: Capacity is how much a resource can handle in a period: container slots on a vessel, kilograms on a flight, trucks per day, pallet positions in a warehouse, declarations a broker can process.
items.definition_ar: السعة هي ما يستطيع مورد ما التعامل معه في فترة: مساحات حاويات على سفينة، أوزان على رحلة طيران، شاحنات يوميًا، مواقع منصات في مخزن، أو إقرارات يستطيع المخلص إنجازها.
items.explanation: When demand nears capacity, delays grow faster than volume (queues): a port at 90% yard utilisation is much slower than one at 70%. Booked space can still be lost — cargo is 'rolled' when a sailing is overbooked.

items.definition: Demand planning estimates future demand from history, known events and market information, so purchasing, inventory and logistics capacity can be planned ahead.
items.definition_ar: تخطيط الطلب هو تقدير الطلب المستقبلي من البيانات السابقة والأحداث المعروفة ومعلومات السوق لتخطيط المشتريات والمخزون والسعة اللوجستية مسبقًا.
items.explanation: Forecasts are always wrong by some amount; good planning measures the error and sizes safety stock and lead times to it. Sales and operations planning (S&OP) is the monthly process that turns the forecast into an agreed plan.

items.definition: A purchase order (PO) is the buyer's formal, numbered commitment to buy stated goods or services from a supplier at stated prices, quantities, delivery dates and terms.
items.explanation: Once the supplier accepts it, the PO is the reference that the shipment, the invoice, the goods receipt and the payment are matched against. Its delivery terms usually name the Incoterms rule and the delivery point, which decide who arranges and pays for each leg.
items.example: PO 4500123 for 12 hydraulic pumps, FCA Antwerp, delivery by 15 November.
misconceptions: A PO is not an invoice: it commits to buy; the invoice asks to be paid.

items.definition: A supplier (vendor) is the company that sells and provides the goods or services a buyer purchases.
items.explanation: In international trade the supplier is usually the seller and often the shipper; under EXW the buyer collects from the supplier's premises, under D-rules the supplier delivers to the destination named.

items.definition: Supplier lead time is the time from placing an order with a supplier until the goods are ready for dispatch (or delivered, if the supplier delivers).
items.explanation: It is one part of total replenishment lead time, which also includes transport, clearance and receiving. Plans that use the quoted figure instead of the observed one underestimate stock needs when suppliers run late.

items.definition: Goods receipt is recording that ordered goods have physically arrived and been checked against the purchase order — items, quantities and condition — usually in the buyer's ERP.
items.explanation: The receipt confirms delivery for the PO and is one of the three documents in a three-way match. Short, damaged or wrong items are recorded at receipt so that claims and payment adjustments can follow.

items.definition: A three-way match checks that the purchase order, the goods receipt and the supplier's invoice agree on items, quantities and prices before the invoice is paid.
items.explanation: A mismatch — invoiced more than received, a price above the PO — stops payment until it is explained. Freight invoices are often checked the same way against the booking or rate agreement (freight audit).

items.definition: A backorder is the part of an order that cannot be supplied now because the item is out of stock, kept open to be supplied when stock arrives.
items.explanation: Backorders lower fill rate and OTIF. Track their age: an old backorder is often a forgotten one.

items.definition: A partial shipment is the dispatch of only part of an order, with the rest following later in one or more further shipments.
items.explanation: Partial shipments must be allowed by the order or the letter of credit when one is used. Each part has its own transport document, and the order is complete only when every part is received — which is why one PO can show several AWBs or B/Ls.
misconceptions: A partial shipment is not the same as this platform's 'Partial' status, which is about dates written to the Hub.

items.definition: Safety stock is extra inventory held to cover variation in demand and in replenishment lead time, so that stock-outs stay below an accepted level.
items.explanation: A common formula, assuming normally distributed daily demand and a fixed lead time, is z × σ(daily demand) × √(lead time in days), where z is set by the target service level. The service level is a business choice — ATLAS does not assume one.
limitations: The simple formula ignores lead-time variability; with variable lead times a combined formula is needed.

items.definition: The reorder point is the stock level at which a new replenishment order is placed: expected demand during the replenishment lead time plus safety stock.
items.explanation: Reorder point = average daily demand × lead time (days) + safety stock. If the real lead time is longer than the one used — a slow supplier, a transshipment, a customs hold — stock runs out before the order arrives.
items.example: 20 units/day, 15-day lead time, 60 units safety stock: reorder at 20 × 15 + 60 = 360 units.

items.definition: FIFO (first in, first out) issues the oldest stock first; FEFO (first expired, first out) issues the stock that expires soonest first.
items.explanation: FEFO matters for goods with a shelf life — lubricants, filters with seals, batteries, chemicals. Picking that ignores it leaves old stock to expire on the shelf.

items.definition: A cycle count is counting a subset of stock locations on a rolling schedule, instead of a full stocktake, to keep inventory records accurate.
items.explanation: High-value or fast-moving items are counted more often. A count difference is investigated (wrong pick, unrecorded receipt, damage) before the record is adjusted.

items.definition: These are the core warehouse steps: receiving checks goods in, putaway stores them in a recorded location, picking takes ordered items from their locations, and packing prepares them for dispatch.
items.explanation: Errors at putaway (a wrong location) show up later as a 'missing' item at picking. Dwell between steps is where warehouse time is lost.

items.definition: A bonded warehouse is a customs-approved store where imported goods can be held without paying import duties and taxes until they are released for home use, re-exported or moved under customs control.
items.explanation: It defers the duty payment and allows goods to wait for an order or a document. The goods stay under customs control, and the operator answers to customs for them; the conditions and time limits are national rules.
limitations: Whether and how long goods can stay, and what may be done to them there, depends on the country's customs law.

items.definition: A return merchandise authorisation (RMA) is the approval and reference a customer must obtain before sending goods back, so the return can be received, inspected and credited or repaired.
items.explanation: Returns are part of reverse logistics. Cross-border returns need their own export and import formalities; returned goods may qualify for duty relief only if the country's rules and the documents support it.

items.definition: Critical slow-moving spares are parts that are rarely used but stop a machine when needed (final drives, major hydraulic components); their demand is intermittent, so normal forecast-and-reorder-point methods set stock badly.
items.definition_ar: قطع الغيار الحرجة بطيئة الحركة هي قطع بتتطلب نادرًا لكن غيابها بيوقف المعدة؛ طلبها متقطع، فطرق التنبؤ ونقطة إعادة الطلب العادية بتظبط المخزون غلط.
items.explanation: Decide them by risk, not by average usage: compare the cost of the machine being down for the replenishment lead time with the cost of holding the part. Common practice: classify criticality (for example vital / essential / desirable), hold a minimum of one (or a small min/max) for parts whose downtime cost is high and whose lead time is long, set a target service level per class, and use methods built for intermittent demand (such as Croston-type forecasting) rather than a plain average. Pool stock across branches or agree supplier or dealer-network availability where possible, and review the installed base: a part is only critical while machines that need it are in the field.

items.definition: In inventory planning, the service level is the target probability of not running out during a replenishment cycle (cycle service level); it sets how much safety stock is held.
items.definition_ar: مستوى الخدمة في تخطيط المخزون هو احتمال إنك ما يخلصش منك المخزون خلال دورة إعادة الطلب، وعلى أساسه بيتحدد مخزون الأمان.
items.explanation: It is not the same as fill rate, which measures the share of demand actually served from stock. Higher service levels need disproportionately more safety stock, so targets are usually set per class of item (higher for critical or high-margin parts, lower for cheap or easily sourced ones).
